newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Eastern Europe advertisers urged to self-regulate.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Europe advertisers urged to self-regulate.

text.p: Eastern Europe, where growth of the advertising industry is following in lock-step with a rising demand for consumer goods, should continue to allow the advertising industry to self-regulate, a Western European advertising official said on Wednesday.

Christopher Ogden, chairman of the European Advertising Standards Alliance (EASA), told the "West Goes East" conference on advertising self-regulation in Eastern and Central Europe that self-regulation was more efficient than government control.
"We consider self-regulation within a legal framework to be the best method of maintaining high industry standards and ensuring consumer confidence," Ogden said.

"West Goes East," organised by the Czech Republic's self-regulating advertising group, Rada Pro Reklamu, brought together advertisers, manufacturers and government officials from both Eastern and Western Europe.

With the fall of communism and the development of market economies, Central and Eastern Europe have seen rapid growth in the advertising industry, with tobacco companies and makers of consumer products such as laundry detergents and shampoos the most aggressive advertisrs as they seek new markets.

The conference featured speakers from a range of consumer industries, including alcoholic beverages, non-prescription medicines and cosmetics, tobacco and food -- the same industries whose advertising in the West tends to receive the greatest scrutiny.

Ogden, who is also deputy director general of Britain's Advertising Standards Authority, pointed to the success self- regulatory systems in Western European countries such as France and Italy as models for Eastern and Central Europe to follow.

EASA, whose 21 member countries include Eastern Europe nations such as the Slovak Republic and Slovenia as well as members of the European Union, aims to both support and promote self-regulation and coordinate the cross-border complaints system. But Ogden emphasised that the advertising alliance remains acutely aware that just as advertising has an international dimension, the alliance itself must be trans-national.

The advertising industry, however, must maintain a high degree of responsibility if self-regulation is to succeed. "Self-regulation is just that, and if there is to be no cost to the state or the individual consumer in the operation of the system then the industry must demonstrate its commitment by paying what is required," Ogden said.

Within the Czech Republic, Ogden noted two main challenges for self-regulation: the increasing sophistication of commercial practice and changes in public attitudes and sensibilities due to increased social awareness and consumer choice.
